leads.question: On tempo main today (version 1.19.2, evm2 7c9f3b6d) and on the first tag that carries T15, which code paths reached from a CALL inside a user transaction can enter evm2 execute_tx (evm/mod.rs:1399-1420 at e80df9c4, which shares one State and clears its transient map when the nested transaction ends)? Rerun callers.py, and read in particular the T15 TIP-20 route to zone portals (crates/precompiles/src/tip20/mod.rs resolve_transfer and deposit_virtual) and any subblock or zone code added after c0c9372: is the portal deposit a call frame or a dispatched transaction?
leads.why: If an ordinary account can make any precompile dispatch a nested transaction while an unlock is open, the end of that transaction clears IS_UNLOCKED_SLOT, NonzeroDeltaCount and every delta (src/libraries/Lock.sol:8-25, src/libraries/NonzeroDeltaCount.sol, src/libraries/CurrencyDelta.sol). A caller could take first, trigger the nested transaction, and pass the check at src/PoolManager.sol:111 with its debt erased, which takes pooled funds of every pool. Cycles 33 and 34 cleared this only because no production caller exists today; F-135 shows T15 adds TIP-20 routing to portals, so the caller list changes with that release.

leads.question: Given that the official X Layer image compiles keccak-asm and keccak-cache-global through the default features of the okx/reth f60420a reth crate (bin/reth/Cargo.toml default list and the asm-keccak feature, xlayer-reth Cargo.toml line 88), which keccak-asm routine does build.rs select with RUSTFLAGS empty, and does that routine, lifted from the official image, return the sha3 crate hash for the input shapes src uses: 160 bytes for PoolId (src/types/PoolId.sol:14), 58 bytes at offset 12 for the position hash (src/libraries/Position.sol:60), 64 bytes for mapping slots and the transient delta slot (src/libraries/CurrencyDelta.sol), plus lengths 135, 136 and 137 around the rate?
leads.why: A wrong hash at the pool id or position hash would merge or split the ledgers of different users, and the sequencer of X Layer is the only producer. The public endpoint matches on every vector tried, which makes a fault unlikely, but the clearance of cycle 34 rests on a refuted manifest reading.

leads.question: Does the operand class table of the cycle 33 counting inspector (40,940 MegaETH blocks whose state root the public validator reproduced, and the 2,833 traced HyperEVM transactions) contain MULMOD executions with a times b at or above 2^256 and a modulus below 2^128, which is the shape of the remainder at src/libraries/FullMath.sol:48 and of the rounding at src/libraries/SqrtPriceMath.sol:252? If the classes were binned by operand width only, recount by product width from the same logs.
leads.why: Cycle 33 says every operand class the PoolManager can produce occurs on MegaETH, and cycle 34 says three PoolManager MULMOD sites never ran there with a wide product while any account can reach that branch in 22 live MegaETH pools by adding one position. If the class was never executed by any contract in validated blocks, a producer fault there could flip the comparison at src/libraries/SwapMath.sol:69 and pay out in-range token0 of other LPs for almost nothing. One recount from logs on disk settles which of the two statements holds.
